modal-content.p: A SSA-1099 is a tax form issued by the Social Security Administration (SSA) every year to people who received Social Security benefits. Anyone who received Social Security benefits in the tax year should get a SSA-1099 from SSA reporting what was paid.
If you lost or never received your SSA-1099, the Social Security Administration can replace it.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: What Social Security benefits aren’t yet supported in Direct File?

modal-content.p: In Direct File, you can report Social Security benefits, except:

ul.li: if the benefits you repaid exceed the benefits you received by over . We’ll let you know if this situation applies to you.
if you had Social Security benefits paid in lump sum from prior years and you would like to make a lump sum election.

modal-content.p: These situations require filing additional forms and schedules that Direct File doesn’t currently support.
If either of these situations apply, you’ll need to file using another tool. Find other ways to file your taxes.

modal-dialog.modal-heading: How is taxable Social Security calculated?

modal-content.p: To calculate how much of your Social Security benefits are taxable, we start with the amounts from Box 5 (Net benefits for ) from any Forms SSA-1099 you reported
We then use Worksheet 1 in IRS Publication 915.
Taxable Social Security depends on the total amount of net Social Security benefits, other income, and certain deductions/exclusions. The taxable amount is lower than the net benefits.
We’ll figure your deductions next and then calculate your taxable Social Security benefits.
